content.prompt: Use set notation to describe the shaded sets.

spec.description: Three equal overlapping circles, A lower left, B lower right and C above, with short label leaders and no universal-set rectangle.
spec.mathematics: Only membership region 111 in the order A,B,C is shaded.
spec.answerVisibility: The shaded region is supplied question data; its set expression appears only in answers.

answer.worked: The shaded region lies inside all three sets, so it is $A\cap B\cap C$.

spec.description: Three equal overlapping circles with external A, B and C labels and short leaders. Only the portions of C overlapping either lower circle are shaded.
spec.mathematics: Membership regions 101,011,111 in the order A,B,C are shaded equally.
spec.answerVisibility: Shading is supplied; the corresponding expression is hidden from the question.

answer.worked: The shading lies in $C$ and also in $A$ or $B$. Hence the set is $(A\cup B)\cap C$.

spec.description: All of lower-right circle B is shaded, as is the overlap of A and C outside B. Circle labels have short non-arrow leaders.
spec.mathematics: Opaque equal pale fills form B union (A intersection C), so overlapping coverage does not darken any region. Membership regions 010,110,011,101,111 are shaded equally.
spec.answerVisibility: The shaded membership regions are question data.

answer.worked: All of $B$ is shaded, together with the overlap $A\cap C$. Their union is $(A\cap C)\cup B$.

spec.description: All three pairwise overlaps are shaded, including the central triple overlap. Exactly-one-set regions are white.
spec.mathematics: Equal opaque pale fills form the union of all three pairwise intersections; triple coverage stays the same pale tint. Regions 110,101,011,111.
spec.answerVisibility: Shaded regions are visible question givens; the set expression is answer-only.

answer.short:
$(A\cap B)\cup(A\cap C)\cup(B\cap C)$

Combine the three pairwise overlaps.
answer.worked: Each shaded point belongs to at least two sets. The shaded lenses are $A\cap B$, $A\cap C$ and $B\cap C$, so their union is $(A\cap B)\cup(A\cap C)\cup(B\cap C)$.
